svg.text: Not every escape costs the same: severity-graded inspection economics
PCA reconstruction on the synthetic test set - parts graded by displaced intensity, cut points 8 / 15 [A11]
illustrative rates: escaped defect 10 / 35 / 140 EUR by grade, false reject 3 EUR, prevalence 1.5%, per 1,000 parts
minor: 43 parts (29%), 10 EUR each
major: 72 parts (48%), 35 EUR each
critical: 35 parts (23%), 140 EUR each
A - the bill: graded escapes vs one flat escape rate
Expected cost (EUR per 1,000 parts)
both models recommend the same operating point: 0.45% of parts pulled
solid - graded escapes [A11]: 509 EUR/1,000 (+39%)
dashed - one flat escape rate [A4]: 368 EUR/1,000
the point moves only once a critical escape is worth 259 EUR (7.4x [A4]) -> 1.83% pulled
B - who actually escapes: share of each grade the screen catches
Share of that grade caught
Reject rate (share of parts pulled for manual inspection) - both panels
major: 42% caught (AUC 0.819)
critical: 34% caught (AUC 0.706)
minor: 7% caught (AUC 0.746)
recommended point
The critical grade is the one the screen ranks worst (AUC 0.706) and the one priced highest: at the recommended point it is 2.3 of 10.5 escaped parts but 63% of the escape bill.
Grading changes what the line should EXPECT TO PAY long before it changes where the line should RUN.
Severity index, per-grade rates and AUCs are MEASURED on the synthetic test set; cut points and per-grade costs are illustrative labelled constants [A11]. Full grid: severity.csv / Severity sheet.
